quarterly_data.signal: Q4 2025 results (call): organic sales growth of 2.2% (Safety & Industrial +3.8%, Transportation & Electronics +2.4%, Consumer down 2.2%); adjusted operating margin 21.1%, up 140 basis points; adjusted EPS $1.83, an increase of 9%, above the top end of the guidance range; adjusted free cash flow $1.3 billion (conversion of approximately 130%). A $55 million transformation charge was excluded from adjusted results. CFO said momentum in all three business segments contributed to a higher ending backlog compared to last year.

quarterly_data.signal: FY2025 results: organic sales growth of 2.1%, accelerating from 1.5% in the first half to 2.7% in the second; adjusted operating margin 23.4%, up 200 basis points; adjusted EPS grew double digits to $8.06; free cash flow conversion slightly above 100%; $4.8 billion returned to shareholders ($1.6 billion dividends, $3.2 billion gross share repurchases). Safety & Industrial grew 3.2% and Transportation & Electronics grew 2%. China grew mid-single digit on general industrials and electronics bonding solutions, momentum that more than offset the fourth-quarter shift in smartphones from China to other parts of Asia. Management said it is progressing ahead of its medium-term (Investor Day) commitments of "a billion-dollar growth over macro and a 25% operating margin by 2027".
quarterly_data.figure: organic sales growth 2.1%; adjusted operating margin 23.4% (up 200 basis points); adjusted EPS $8.06; $4.8 billion returned to shareholders

quarterly_data.signal: Initial FY2026 guidance: organic sales growth of approximately 3%, adjusted operating margin expansion of 70 to 80 basis points, EPS of $8.5 to $8.7, free cash flow conversion greater than 100%, and gross share repurchase of approximately $2.5 billion. Sales expected to accelerate in all business groups, with Consumer returning to growth; business groups to expand margins over $450 million or 100 basis points, including $875 million from volume growth and net productivity, partly offset by PFAS, stranded-cost and tariff headwinds and growth/productivity investments rising to $225 million. Pricing expected at about eighty basis points in 2026, a lot of it in Safety & Industrial. Macro planned similar to 2025; watch items are the US consumer recovery, auto build rates and consumer electronics. Cadence: Q1 sales growth for Safety & Industrial plus Transportation & Electronics higher than 3% with high single-digit EPS growth; EPS equal between the two halves. Possible new European tariffs are not in guidance and could be a $30 million, $40 million impact this year.
quarterly_data.figure: organic sales growth approximately 3%; margin expansion 70 to 80 basis points; EPS $8.5 to $8.7; gross share repurchase approximately $2.5 billion

quarterly_data.signal: Electronics (semiconductor and data center exposure): Q4 electronics organic growth was in the mid-single digits excluding PFAS (the reported sub-segment tables still include PFAS), and electronics continued to gain share on "strong demand for our film technologies and optically clear adhesives". Consumer-electronics macro looks "a little bit more flattish", but CEO Bill Brown said "when we add in electronic in semiconductor, data center, all electronics to be up mid-single digits here coming into 2026, similar to what we saw last year". 3M supplies adhesives and films for foldable and debondable devices and is pushing from its premium-heavy mix (80/20 or 70/30 premium to mainstream) into the mainstream market, penetrating China OEMs and Asia OEMs with new products; "We are not seeing it being more margin dilutive."
quarterly_data.figure: all electronics (incl. semiconductor, data center) expected up mid-single digits in 2026; Q4 electronics up mid-single digits excluding PFAS

quarterly_data.signal: Innovation and portfolio pivot: 284 new products launched in 2025 (up 68% versus 2024), with 350 launches expected in 2026; sales of products launched in the last five years were up 23% for the year; new product vitality index ended at 13%. Asked what share of the business sits in priority verticals, Bill Brown said "a little bit north of 60%", with probably 80% of R&D spend aligned to new product introductions in the priority verticals; about 10% of the company would be in places that are "more commodity-like", and 3M will probably think about what to do with those businesses over time while pivoting organically and inorganically toward priority verticals. 2026 outgrowth over the macro is seen at $300 million or more, roughly half from new products and half from commercial excellence (2025: about $150 million).
